docsFacts:
Sources fetched 2026-10-18: https://twelvedata.com/docs (time_series section), its markdown copy https://twelvedata.com/docs/llms/market-data/time-series.md, and the OpenAPI spec https://api.twelvedata.com/doc/swagger/openapi.json.

TIME_SERIES
- Cost: "1 per symbol".
- interval: 1min, 5min, 15min, 30min, 45min, 1h, 2h, 4h, 8h, 1day, 1week, 1month.
- outputsize: "Supports values in the range from 1 to 5000. Default 30 when no date parameters are set, otherwise set to maximum".
- order: asc or desc. Default is desc.
- timezone: "Exchange" (default), "UTC", or an IANA name (case-sensitive). The docs say: "only applicable for intraday intervals ... For intervals of 1day, 1week, or 1month, the timezone parameter is ignored, and data is strictly returned in the Exchange local time".
- date: an exact date (for example 2021-10-27), or "today" / "yesterday".
- start_date: "Can be used separately and together with end_date. Format 2006-01-02 or 2006-01-02T15:04:05".
  - Default location: "Forex and Cryptocurrencies - UTC; Stocks - where exchange is located".
  - "If timezone is given then, start_date and end_date will be used in the specified location".
- end_date: "The ending date and time for data selection".
- format: JSON (default) or CSV. CSV delimiter defaults to ';'.
- dp: decimal places, 0 to 11.
- values[].datetime: "when the bar with specified interval was opened". OHLC values are returned as strings.

WHAT THE DOCS LEAVE OUT, AND WHAT WE MEASURED
The docs do not say whether end_date is inclusive, or which end outputsize trims. Support article https://support.twelvedata.com/en/articles/5656039-how-to-get-historical-prices says end_date "defines the maximum possible datetime value for the time series. The number of rows is entirely determined by the outputsize parameter". Its end_date-only example returns "the last five records". It also says "Try to get it once, cache and update it later".

Measured with the demo key:
- start_date and end_date are both inclusive.
- When a range holds more bars than outputsize, the OLDEST bars are dropped. The API returns the newest N bars up to end_date, then sorts them by `order`.
- A date-only end_date means 00:00:00 of that day, and that bar is included.
- A dated request with no outputsize returned all 121 bars, not 30.
- Both the YYYY-MM-DD and the YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS formats work.
- Forex bars have no volume field.
- Forex meta has currency_base, currency_quote and type="Physical Currency", but no exchange_timezone.

EARLIEST_TIMESTAMP
- Docs: "provides the earliest available date and time for a specified financial instrument at a given data interval".
- Parameters: symbol, figi, isin or cusip; interval (required); exchange; mic_code; timezone.
- Returns {datetime, unix_time}. Cost: 1 per request.

API_USAGE (https://twelvedata.com/docs/llms/advanced/api-usage.md)
- Cost: 1 per request.
- Parameters: format, delimiter, timezone (default UTC).
- Fields:
  - timestamp
  - current_usage: "Number of requests made in last minute"
  - plan_limit: "Your personal API limit (requests/minute) depending on the plan"
  - daily_usage and plan_daily_limit: "Returned only when the plan has a daily limit"
  - plan_category: "Plan category name". The docs example value is "enterprise".

CREDITS AND HEADERS
- Pricing page: "API credits quota will be reset each minute, and there are no hidden extra data weights unless explicitly stated", so bar count does not change the cost.
- https://support.twelvedata.com/en/articles/5615854-credits:
  - The Basic daily quota "resets to 800 at midnight UTC (00:00:00)".
  - "paid plans have no daily limits".
  - "Each API request returns api-credits-used and api-credits-left in response headers."
- https://support.twelvedata.com/en/articles/5713553-control-over-api-usage: "Adding these two values provides the total credit limit for your plan".
- These headers were NOT present on any demo-key response.

ERRORS
- Error body is JSON {code, message, status:"error"}, and the HTTP status equals the code. Measured: a 401 error came back as HTTP 401.
- Example 429 message from the OpenAPI spec: "You have run out of API credits for the current minute. 1000 API credits were used, with the current limit being 987. Wait for the next minute or consider upgrading your plan at https://twelvedata.com/pricing".

AUTHENTICATION
- Either the apikey query parameter or the header "Authorization: apikey <key>". The docs mark the header as recommended.

HISTORY DEPTH
- https://twelvedata.com/exchanges/physical_currency (forex): "Basic+". Intraday "Starting September 20, 2019 with intervals between 1 minute and 8 hours". Daily data from Jan 1, 1980. Trial symbol is EUR/USD.
- https://twelvedata.com/exchanges/commodity: "Grow+" / "Venture+". Intraday from January 9, 2020. Trial symbol is XAU/USD.
- https://twelvedata.com/markets/300755/commodity/xau-usd: "/time_series data via our API — starting from the Basic plan and above".
- The pricing pages state no history-depth limit per plan.

licensing:
Wawe Journal is a commercial SaaS: users pay for premium through NOWPayments. Its backtest page shows Twelve Data candles to those users. On Twelve Data's published terms, that needs a Business plan. No Individual plan covers it.

PRICING PAGES
- https://twelvedata.com/pricing: "Pricing for Individual - Access the data for personal, internal, and non-commercial purposes."
- Rights listed per Individual plan:
  - Basic: "Internal non-display usage".
  - Grow (and Pro, which inherits it): "Internal display data access".
  - Ultra: adds "Internal non-display data access".
- https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business: "Pricing for Business - Access data for commercial, external, and professional use."
  - Venture: "ideal for companies showcasing data on client-facing apps or websites" and "External display data access".
  - Enterprise: "External distribution market data".

TERMS OF USE (https://twelvedata.com/terms, "Last updated: January 1, 2026")
- Definition: "'Internal Use' means use solely for Customer's internal business purposes and not for redistribution or external commercial purposes."
- 2.1: the license is "solely for Internal Use ... except as otherwise expressly permitted by your Subscription Tier, Data add-ons, or a separate written agreement".
- 2.2(e): "Redistribute or provide external display of Data only if and as expressly authorized by a Redistribution Rights Add-On or separate written agreement with Twelve Data (including compliance with attribution requirements)".
- 2.4: "Certain Subscription Tiers or Data Add-ons may permit limited redistribution or external display of Data, subject to additional terms, attribution requirements ... Contact sales@twelvedata.com".
- 2.3 restrictions:
  - "(l) Use Free Tier data for commercial purposes"
  - "(g) Store or cache Data beyond permitted timeframes specified in the Documentation". The docs pages reviewed state no specific timeframe. The docs best practices say "Cache responses for frequently accessed data", and the support article says "get it once, cache".
- 16.1: "Customer may retain Data only: (a) For duration permitted by subscription".
- 16.2: "Upon termination or expiration: (a) All Data must be deleted within 30 days".
- 5.6(b): "No commercial use permitted during Free Trial".

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR US
1. The Basic (free) plan and every Individual tier are not licensed for this app's current or planned use.
2. Venture, from $149/mo, is the minimum listed tier with external display. Serving cached raw data as downloads or exports, or through an API, would move toward 'distribution', which needs Enterprise or a redistribution add-on.
3. The shared Supabase candle cache is allowed only while a subscription is active. It must be deletable within 30 days of termination, so tag cached rows with their source and keep a purge routine.
4. Before going live, the owner should confirm in writing with sales@twelvedata.com that "cache once in our DB, display to all logged-in users in a replay chart" is covered by Venture, and ask what attribution is required.

This is a reading of the published terms, not legal advice.

howToVerifyPlan:
These checks are safe and read-only. Run them from the owner's own machine. Do not call get-candles, do not touch Supabase, and do not paste the key into the repo or chat.

1) DASHBOARD
Sign in at https://twelvedata.com and open the account dashboard at https://twelvedata.com/account. API keys are at https://twelvedata.com/account/api-keys. The current plan and its credits appear there; the pricing FAQ says plans are changed "from your Dashboard". Make sure this is the account that issued the key stored in the Supabase Edge Function secret TWELVE_DATA_API_KEY. That value cannot be read back from the repo.

2) API CHECK (costs 1 API credit)
Use the header form so the key does not end up in URLs or logs.
- Git Bash: read -s TD_KEY; curl -s -i -H "Authorization: apikey $TD_KEY" https://api.twelvedata.com/api_usage
- PowerShell: use curl.exe with the same arguments.

Read these fields from the JSON:
- plan_category: the plan name. The docs example value is "enterprise".
- plan_limit: credits per minute.
- daily_usage and plan_daily_limit: present ONLY when the plan has a daily cap, which means Basic with 800.
- current_usage: credits used in the last minute.

Also read the response headers api-credits-used and api-credits-left. Their sum equals the per-minute limit.

How to map the result:
- 8 per minute with an 800 daily limit: Basic.
- 55 / 144 / 377: Grow.
- 610 / 987 / 1,597: Pro. Venture uses 610 and 1,597 too, so check plan_category.
- 2,584 / 4,181 / 10,946: Ultra. Venture uses 2,584 and Enterprise uses 10,946, so check plan_category.
plan_category tells individual and business plans apart.

3) GOLD ACCESS (optional, 1 credit)
curl -s -H "Authorization: apikey $TD_KEY" "https://api.twelvedata.com/symbol_search?symbol=XAU/USD&show_plan=true"
Read data[].access.plan (individual) and data[].access.plan_business. The docs describe this as "Info on which plan symbol is available".

UNTIL THIS IS DONE
Design for Basic as the worst case:
- 8 credits per minute, global across all users.
- 800 credits per day.
- Assume no commodities.
Plan the purchase around Venture (610 per minute, no daily cap), which is required for licensing anyway.
report:
TWELVE DATA CHECK FOR THE BACKTEST DATA LAYER
Read-only work. I made exactly 4 calls with the public "demo" key and never sent any other key. I did not touch Supabase or any Edge Function.

1) DATE RANGES: SUPPORTED
time_series accepts start_date, end_date, date, outputsize (1-5000), order (asc/desc, default desc), timezone (Exchange by default, UTC, or an IANA name) and format (JSON or CSV). Source: https://twelvedata.com/docs/llms/market-data/time-series.md.

What the live tests showed:
- start_date and end_date are both inclusive. 10:00-12:00 UTC returned 121 M1 bars with no gaps.
- When a range holds more bars than outputsize, the OLDEST bars are cut. outputsize=5 over 2026-10-14..2026-10-15 returned 23:56..00:00, and order=asc was applied after the cut.
- A dated request with no outputsize returns up to the maximum (5000), not 30.
- Both date formats work: 2006-01-02 and 2006-01-02T15:04:05.
- A date-only end_date means 00:00:00 of that day.
- timezone=UTC returns UTC bar-open times. timezone is ignored for 1day/1week/1month, which come back in exchange-local time.
- Forex bars have no volume field, and forex meta has no exchange_timezone.
- earliest_timestamp for EUR/USD 1min is 2020-04-07 06:54 UTC. The forex exchange page says intraday data from 2019-09-20; the commodity exchange page says from 2020-01-09.
- Cost is 1 credit per symbol per request, regardless of how many bars come back.
- api_usage (1 credit) returns timestamp, current_usage, plan_limit (credits per minute), daily_usage and plan_daily_limit (only on plans with a daily cap), and plan_category.
- Errors come back with the matching HTTP status. The demo key on XAU/USD gave HTTP 401.
- No api-credits-used or api-credits-left headers appeared on demo responses. Twelve Data support says every real-key request carries them, and that their sum is the plan's per-minute limit.
- The OpenAPI example 429 message states the limit: "...1000 API credits were used, with the current limit being 987...".

2) PLANS (pricing pages fetched 2026-10-18)
Individual plans (https://twelvedata.com/pricing):
- Basic: free, 8 credits/min, 800/day.
- Grow: 55, 144 or 377 credits/min, $29-79/mo.
- Pro: 610, 987 or 1,597 credits/min, $99-229/mo.
- Ultra: 2,584, 4,181 or 10,946 credits/min, $329-999/mo.

Business plans (https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business):
- Venture: 610, 1,597 or 2,584 credits/min, $149-499/mo.
- Enterprise: 10,946 credits/min or more, from $1,099/mo.

Only Basic has a daily cap. Forex is included on every plan. Commodities market data (gold) is NOT included on Basic, though XAU/USD is the commodity trial symbol and its market page says time_series is available "from the Basic plan". The pricing pages state no history-depth limit per plan.

3) LICENSING
Individual plans are "for personal, internal, and non-commercial purposes", with at most "Internal display".
Terms 2.3(l) forbid "Use Free Tier data for commercial purposes".
External display is listed only on Business plans: Venture, which is "ideal for companies showcasing data on client-facing apps or websites".
Terms 16.1 and 16.2 allow keeping data only for the length of the subscription, and require deleting it within 30 days of termination.
So the shared Supabase cache is fine while subscribed, but it needs a purge path. The owner should confirm the cache-plus-replay use case and attribution with sales@twelvedata.com.

4) WHICH PLAN WE USE: CANNOT BE DETERMINED
Nothing in the repo, git history, .env.example, wrangler.toml, PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md, .agent/ or the DB snapshots names the plan.
The function's own defaults match no Twelve Data tier: RATE_LIMIT_MAX=30 (supabase/functions/get-candles/index.ts:7) and the 10-500 outputsize clamp (index.ts:216-217).
The owner can check either way:
- the Twelve Data dashboard (https://twelvedata.com/account), or
- api_usage with their own key and the "Authorization: apikey" header, reading plan_category, plan_limit and plan_daily_limit (details in howToVerifyPlan).
Worst case to design for is Basic: 8 credits/min, global per key, 800/day.

5) DOES GET-CANDLES REVEAL THE PLAN? NO
- index.ts:226-235: any non-2xx upstream response is replaced with {error:'Data service unavailable', status} without reading the body, and index.ts:227 logs only the status code. Twelve Data sends real HTTP statuses (test 4), so a 429 message that names the limit is lost.
- index.ts:240-261: the data.status==='error' branch would forward data.message (lines 254-260) and log it (line 241). It only runs on HTTP 2xx error bodies, which the test suggests do not happen. 401/403 are turned into a generic 503 (lines 244-252).
- index.ts:264-291: the success response is a new object with the function's own X-RateLimit-* headers from its in-memory limiter (lines 33, 63-86, 172-174, 277-281). Upstream headers are never read or forwarded.
- Browser side: src/pages/backtest.astro:385-388 throws the generic supabase-js error, which is shown at backtest.astro:653.

6) DESIGN IMPLICATIONS
- The credit budget belongs to the API key and is shared by all users. Use a global DB-backed throttle with configurable defaults of 8/min and 800/day, not the per-isolate, per-user limiter.
- Fetch M1 data with timezone=UTC and outputsize=5000, in one of two ways:
  - Page backward, setting end_date to the oldest returned bar minus 1 minute.
  - Use fixed windows of 3 calendar days or less (at most 4,320 bars).
  Record coverage per symbol, interval and UTC day.
- Build higher timeframes from M1 with an explicit session boundary.
- Sizing:
  - A forex week is about 7,200 M1 bars, or about 374k per year. That is about 75 calls per symbol per year (about 122 with 3-day windows).
  - From April 2020 to now is about 2.4M bars, about 490 calls per symbol.
  - For 8 symbols that is about 3,900 calls: about 5 days of a Basic daily quota, about 71 minutes on Grow-55, or about 6.5 minutes on Venture-610.
  - JSON is about 104 bytes per bar, so about 0.5 MB per call. CSV is smaller.
  - On Basic, fetch lazily as users need data.
- Log api-credits-used/left and upstream error messages on the server only. Send the key in the header rather than the query string (index.ts:220).

7) SIDE FINDINGS IN CURRENT CODE
- The page sends '15m' (src/pages/backtest.astro:234), but INTERVAL_MAP has no '15m' key (index.ts:20-30), so 15-minute requests silently return daily bars (index.ts:210-213). The first version of the function (git 238e42e, supabase/get-candles/index.ts:13) did map '15m'.
- '1m' maps to '1month' (index.ts:29).
- The client parses 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss' with new Date() as browser-local time (backtest.astro:394), while the function sends no timezone (index.ts:220).
- The function forwards only symbol, interval and outputsize (index.ts:190, 220).
